review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

5:1.sourceText: οἴδαμεν γὰρ ὅτι ἐὰν ἡ ἐπίγειος ἡμῶν οἰκία τοῦ σκήνους καταλυθῇ, οἰκοδομὴν ἐκ Θεοῦ ἔχομεν, οἰκίαν ἀχειροποίητον αἰώνιον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
5:1.targetText: Now we know that if the earthly tent we live in is dismantled, we have a building from God, an eternal house in heaven, not built by human hands.

groups.note: γάρ ("for") is rendered Now.
BSB renders ἡμῶν οἰκία ("our house") as the tent "we live in".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB gives one "the" for this phrase, linked to τοῦ σκήνους ("of the tent").
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:2.sourceText: καὶ γὰρ ἐν τούτῳ στενάζομεν, τὸ οἰκητήριον ἡμῶν τὸ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐπενδύσασθαι ἐπιποθοῦντες,
5:2.targetText: For in this tent we groan, longing to be clothed with our heavenly dwelling,

groups.note: καὶ γάρ ("for indeed") is rendered For.
τὸ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ("the one from heaven") is rendered heavenly.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the tent that τούτῳ ("this") refers to.

5:3.sourceText: εἴ γε καὶ ἐνδυσάμενοι οὐ γυμνοὶ εὑρεθησόμεθα.
5:3.targetText: because when we are clothed, we will not be found naked.

groups.note: εἴ γε ("if indeed") is rendered because.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the subject for the participle.

5:4.sourceText: καὶ γὰρ οἱ ὄντες ἐν τῷ σκήνει στενάζομεν βαρούμενοι ἐφ’ ᾧ οὐ θέλομεν ἐκδύσασθαι ἀλλ’ ἐπενδύσασθαι, ἵνα καταποθῇ τὸ θνητὸν ὑπὸ τῆς ζωῆς.
5:4.targetText: So while we are in this tent, we groan under our burdens, because we do not wish to be unclothed but clothed, so that our mortality may be swallowed up by life.

groups.note: καὶ γάρ ("for indeed") is rendered So.
The article with the participle ὄντες ("being") is rendered while … are.
βαρούμενοι ("being burdened") is rendered under our burdens.
ἐφ’ ᾧ ("on the ground that") is rendered because.
The article is used as a possessive and rendered our.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the subject for the participle.

5:5.sourceText: ὁ δὲ κατεργασάμενος ἡμᾶς εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο Θεός, ὁ δοὺς ἡμῖν τὸν ἀρραβῶνα τοῦ Πνεύματος.
5:5.targetText: And God has prepared us for this very purpose and has given us the Spirit as a pledge of what is to come.

groups.note: The article with the participle κατεργασάμενος ("having prepared") is rendered has prepared.
The article with the participle δούς ("having given") is rendered has given.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the second description of God with and; the Greek has none.
English supplies what the pledge looks forward to.
English supplies the noun; the Greek has the neuter "this very thing".

5:6.sourceText: Θαρροῦντες οὖν πάντοτε καὶ εἰδότες ὅτι ἐνδημοῦντες ἐν τῷ σώματι ἐκδημοῦμεν ἀπὸ τοῦ Κυρίου·
5:6.targetText: Therefore we are always confident, although we know that while we are at home in the body, we are away from the Lord.

groups.note: καί ("and") is rendered although.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the subject for the participle.
English supplies the subject for the participle.
English supplies the subject for the participle.

5:7.sourceText: διὰ πίστεως γὰρ περιπατοῦμεν, οὐ διὰ εἴδους·
5:7.targetText: For we walk by faith, not by sight.

5:8.sourceText: θαρροῦμεν δὲ καὶ εὐδοκοῦμεν μᾶλλον ἐκδημῆσαι ἐκ τοῦ σώματος καὶ ἐνδημῆσαι πρὸς τὸν Κύριον.
5:8.targetText: We are confident, then, and would prefer to be away from the body and at home with the Lord.

groups.note: δέ is rendered then.
εὐδοκοῦμεν μᾶλλον ("we are well pleased rather") is rendered would prefer.

5:9.sourceText: διὸ καὶ φιλοτιμούμεθα, εἴτε ἐνδημοῦντες εἴτε ἐκδημοῦντες, εὐάρεστοι αὐτῷ εἶναι.
5:9.targetText: So we aspire to please Him, whether we are here in this body or away from it.

groups.note: ἐνδημοῦντες ("being at home") is rendered are here.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the subject for the participle.
English supplies the body from verses 6 and 8; this verse does not name it.
English supplies the body as what we are away from; this verse does not name it.

5:10.sourceText: τοὺς γὰρ πάντας ἡμᾶς φανερωθῆναι δεῖ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ βήματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἵνα κομίσηται ἕκαστος τὰ διὰ τοῦ σώματος πρὸς ἃ ἔπραξεν, εἴτε ἀγαθὸν εἴτε φαῦλον.
5:10.targetText: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive his due for the things done in the body, whether good or bad.

groups.note: κομίσηται ("receive back, be repaid") is rendered may receive his due.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB renders "the things" once, with the relative ἃ.

5:11.sourceText: Εἰδότες οὖν τὸν φόβον τοῦ Κυρίου ἀνθρώπους πείθομεν, Θεῷ δὲ πεφανερώμεθα· ἐλπίζω δὲ καὶ ἐν ταῖς συνειδήσεσιν ὑμῶν πεφανερῶσθαι.
5:11.targetText: Therefore, since we know what it means to fear the Lord, we try to persuade men. What we are is clear to God, and I hope it is clear to your conscience as well.

groups.note: The noun φόβον ("fear") is rendered as a verb.
πεφανερώμεθα ("we have been made known") is rendered What we are is clear.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves this δέ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the subject for the participle.
English adds a frame before to fear.
English supplies the subject for the infinitive.

5:12.sourceText: οὐ πάλιν ἑαυτοὺς συνιστάνομεν ὑμῖν, ἀλλὰ ἀφορμὴν διδόντες ὑμῖν καυχήματος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, ἵνα ἔχητε πρὸς τοὺς ἐν προσώπῳ καυχωμένους καὶ μὴ ἐν καρδίᾳ.
5:12.targetText: We are not commending ourselves to you again. Instead, we are giving you an occasion to be proud of us, so that you can answer those who take pride in appearances rather than in the heart.

groups.note: ἔχητε πρός ("you may have something toward") is rendered you can answer.
The article with the participle καυχωμένους ("boasting") is rendered those who take pride.
καὶ μή ("and not") is rendered rather than.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the subject for the participle.

5:13.sourceText: εἴτε γὰρ ἐξέστημεν, Θεῷ· εἴτε σωφρονοῦμεν, ὑμῖν.
5:13.targetText: If we are out of our mind, it is for God; if we are of sound mind, it is for you.

targetPhrases.text: we are out of our mind

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves γάρ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject and copula; the clause has no verb.
English supplies a subject and copula; the clause has no verb.

5:14.sourceText: ἡ γὰρ ἀγάπη τοῦ Χριστοῦ συνέχει ἡμᾶς, κρίναντας τοῦτο, ὅτι εἷς ὑπὲρ πάντων ἀπέθανεν· ἄρα οἱ πάντες ἀπέθανον·
5:14.targetText: For Christ’s love compels us, because we are convinced that One died for all, therefore all died.

groups.note: κρίναντας ("having concluded") is rendered because … are convinced.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves τοῦτο ("this") untranslated before the that-clause.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the subject for the participle.

5:15.sourceText: καὶ ὑπὲρ πάντων ἀπέθανεν ἵνα οἱ ζῶντες μηκέτι ἑαυτοῖς ζῶσιν ἀλλὰ τῷ ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν ἀποθανόντι καὶ ἐγερθέντι.
5:15.targetText: And He died for all, that those who live should no longer live for themselves, but for Him who died for them and was raised again.

groups.note: The article with the participle ζῶντες ("living") is rendered those who live.
The article with the participle ἀποθανόντι ("having died") is rendered for Him who died.

5:16.sourceText: Ὥστε ἡμεῖς ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν οὐδένα οἴδαμεν κατὰ σάρκα· εἰ καὶ ἐγνώκαμεν κατὰ σάρκα Χριστόν, ἀλλὰ νῦν οὐκέτι γινώσκομεν.
5:16.targetText: So from now on we regard no one according to the flesh. Although we once regarded Christ in this way, we do so no longer.

groups.note: εἰ καί ("even if") is rendered Although.
κατὰ σάρκα ("according to the flesh") is rendered in this way.

unmappedSource.reason: The article with νῦν ("now") has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves ἀλλά ("yet") untranslated.
BSB leaves this νῦν ("now") untranslated before no longer.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds an adverb marking the former state.

5:17.sourceText: ὥστε εἴ τις ἐν Χριστῷ, καινὴ κτίσις· τὰ ἀρχαῖα παρῆλθεν, ἰδοὺ γέγονεν καινά.
5:17.targetText: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the clause has no verb.
English supplies a subject and copula; the clause has no verb.

5:18.sourceText: τὰ δὲ πάντα ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ καταλλάξαντος ἡμᾶς ἑαυτῷ διὰ Χριστοῦ καὶ δόντος ἡμῖν τὴν διακονίαν τῆς καταλλαγῆς,
5:18.targetText: All this is from God, who reconciled us to Himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation:

groups.note: τὰ πάντα ("all things") is rendered All this.
The article with the participle καταλλάξαντος ("having reconciled") is rendered who reconciled.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the clause has no verb.

5:19.sourceText: ὡς ὅτι Θεὸς ἦν ἐν Χριστῷ κόσμον καταλλάσσων ἑαυτῷ, μὴ λογιζόμενος αὐτοῖς τὰ παραπτώματα αὐτῶν, καὶ θέμενος ἐν ἡμῖν τὸν λόγον τῆς καταλλαγῆς.
5:19.targetText: that God was reconciling the world to Himself in Christ, not counting men’s trespasses against them. And He has committed to us the message of reconciliation.

groups.note: ὡς ὅτι ("namely that") is rendered that.
αὐτῶν ("their") is rendered men’s.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the subject for the participle.

5:20.sourceText: Ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ οὖν πρεσβεύομεν ὡς τοῦ Θεοῦ παρακαλοῦντος δι’ ἡμῶν· δεόμεθα ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ, καταλλάγητε τῷ Θεῷ.
5:20.targetText: Therefore we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God were making His appeal through us. We implore you on behalf of Christ: Be reconciled to God.

groups.note: παρακαλοῦντος ("appealing") is rendered were making His appeal.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of We implore.

5:21.sourceText: τὸν μὴ γνόντα ἁμαρτίαν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἁμαρτίαν ἐποίησεν, ἵνα ἡμεῖς γενώμεθα δικαιοσύνη Θεοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ.
5:21.targetText: God made Him who knew no sin to be sin on our behalf, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject that ἐποίησεν ("made") gives only by its ending.
English supplies the infinitive after made.
